descriptionChirho: Plural noun קְלָעִים (qela'im) referring to the woven hangings or curtains used in the construction of the tabernacle courtyard (Exod 27, 35, 38; Num 3:26, 4:26). Eng 'hangings / hangings of,' Spa 'cortinas,' Hin 'परदे,' Arb 'سَتائِرُ,' Kor '휘장들,' Swa 'mapazia.' These 15 occurrences consistently denote the fabric screens enclosing the sacred space.

Plural noun קְלָעִים used to denote the carved panels or leaves of a door/gate structure (1 Kgs 6:34), distinct from the tabernacle curtain usage. Eng 'leaves of,' Spa 'hojas de,' Hin 'पटरे,' Arb 'مِصْرَاعَانِ,' Kor '판들이,' Swa 'vipande.' The Arabic translation uses an entirely different lexeme (مِصْرَاعَانِ 'door-leaves'), confirming this is a semantically distinct sense from the textile 'hangings.'
